_**User (2026-05-06 16:26:15Z)**_

how do i create a new project in codex

---

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-05-06 16:26:20Z)**_

To create a new project for Codex, make a normal project folder first, then open Codex from that folder.

Example:

```bash
mkdir my-new-project
cd my-new-project
git init
codex
```

Then tell Codex what you want to build, for example:

```text
Create a Vite React app here with TypeScript and Tailwind.
```

If you already have a project:

```bash
cd path/to/existing-project
codex
```

Codex works against the current working directory, so the “project” is basically the folder/repo you launch it from.

_**User (2026-05-06 16:27:34Z)**_

the codex extension says add project to use codex why?

---

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-05-06 16:27:40Z)**_

That usually means the Codex extension does not have a workspace/project folder selected yet.

In VS Code, Codex needs an opened folder so it knows which files it is allowed to read and edit. Do this:

1. Open VS Code.
2. Go to `File > Open Folder...`
3. Select your project folder.
4. Then open the Codex extension again.
5. Use `Add project` if it asks, and choose that folder.

If you do not have a project yet, create an empty folder first, then open it in VS Code:

```bash
mkdir my-project
cd my-project
code .
```

Then Codex should be able to attach to that folder.

If you opened only a single file instead of a folder, the extension will often show “Add project” because there is no workspace root.
